answer: Shared-Origin Delay Auction. Each new identity must wait until the next dawn to act, and posting a coordination request requires holding a lantern token whose price rises with the number of identities joining the same window. The protocol measures burst clustering: when many identities appear in one interval, the velvet penalty multiplies the auction price for every participant in that cluster. An attacker running N sybils therefore pays superlinear cost per identity, since crowding the same window forces all of them into the expensive tier.
